Differential diagnosis included multiple hydatid cysts of the anterior abdominal wall, but this was excluded when the indirect hemagglutination test was negative. evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnoses of a large septic vegetation or a papillary hydatid cyst were hypothesized.
Pathology showed a nonspecific inflammation, ischemic necrosis, and focal abscesses which were consistent with IE.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of ruptured papillary muscle

step10_contradiction_notes: Papillary hydatid cyst considered in differential was ruled out by pathology demonstrating infective endocarditis.
rationale: A 26-year-old male presented with prolonged fever and was found to have a mobile mass on the mitral anterolateral papillary muscle. Hydatid cyst of the papillary muscle was hypothesized in the differential diagnosis. Histopathological examination of the excised ruptured papillary muscle during valve replacement revealed nonspecific inflammation, ischemic necrosis, and focal abscesses consistent with infective endocarditis, ruling out hydatid disease.

evidence_items.source_quote: Echinoccocal serology was negative.
At this stage, the differential diagnoses included biliary cyst adenoma and Echinococcal cyst.

step10_contradiction_notes: Suspected echinococcal cyst ruled out by negative serology and absence of hydatid disease on investigation.
rationale: A 55-year-old female presented with epigastric pain and a 9 cm multi-lobulated cystic lesion in segment 8 of the liver. Echinococcal cyst was considered in the differential diagnosis along with biliary cystadenoma. Echinococcal serology was negative, preoperative investigation suggested absence of hydatid disease, and robotic laparoscopic resection was successfully executed, confirming a non-parasitic cystic tumor.

evidence_items.source_quote: The immune-diffusion test for Echinococus multilocularis was negative. The Indirect hemagglutination test and the Elisa test for Echinococcus granulosus were also negative.
The pathology report showed stratified epithelium with fibro-inflammatory reaction in the pericystic zone compatible with splenic epithelial cyst.
evidence_items.test_name: Pathology examination of excised splenic cyst

step10_contradiction_notes: Suspected splenic hydatid cyst ruled out by negative serology and histopathology confirming splenic epithelial cyst.
rationale: A 17-year-old female presented with left upper quadrant pain and a 15 cm splenic cyst with parietal calcifications initially suspected to be hydatid in origin. Immunodiffusion test for E. multilocularis, IHA, and ELISA for E. granulosus were all negative. Following laparotomy and cyst unroofing, the pathology report showed stratified epithelium with fibro-inflammatory reaction compatible with a splenic epithelial cyst, definitively ruling out echinococcosis.

step4_condition_matched: Hydatid cyst of liver (historical treated surgical episode)

evidence_items.source_quote: Cholecystectomy and cystectomy due to hydatid cyst of the liver were performed on a 47-year-old man.

rationale: A 47-year-old male who had previously undergone cholecystectomy and cystectomy for a hydatid cyst of the liver presented with right abdominal pain, fever, and a 6x8 cm hepatic fluid collection. ERCP confirmed a bronchobiliary fistula between the biliary tree and the right lower lung lobe. The hydatid cyst represents a prior treated surgical episode, and no active echinococcal disease was present or evaluated during this care episode.

evidence_items.source_quote: As Echinococcus granulosus is common in Southeastern Turkey, an immunofluorescence assay was performed to check the patient's blood for antigens. In addition, a check of the liver revealed no cysts caused by Echinococcus granulosus.
evidence_items.test_name: Echinococcus granulosus serological and ultrasound workup

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathological examinations revealed a benign renal cyst and benign mesenchymal mass, with an extensive hyalinized area, focal calcifications, and little cellularity on hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of excised abdominal mass

step10_contradiction_notes: Suspected echinococcosis was ruled out by negative serology/imaging and histopathology confirming benign mesenchymal mass.
rationale: A 48-year-old man presented with lumbar pain and LUTS, found to have a 7 cm calcific mass above the bladder. Due to regional endemicity in Turkey, Echinococcus granulosus was investigated via immunofluorescence assay and hepatic imaging and was negative. Laparoscopic excision and histopathology confirmed a benign mesenchymal mass with extensive hyalinization and focal calcifications, definitively ruling out echinococcosis.

step4_condition_matched: Echinococcus granulosus infection (cross-reactive serology, ruled out)

evidence_items.source_quote: the presence of antibodies against E. granulosus was confirmed by ELISA and indirect hemagglutination, but not by a western blot confirmation test. The patient was thoroughly screened for signs of an Echinococcus infection by sonography and CT scans, but no indications of a hydatid cyst were found.
evidence_items.test_name: Western blot confirmation and CT/sonography screening
evidence_items.target_concept: Echinococcus granulosus confirmatory testing and cysts

evidence_items.source_quote: Sequence analysis of the PCR product showed the highest similarity to Italian isolates of D. repens, thus confirming the morphological identification of our isolate as D. repens.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial cross-reactive ELISA/IHA antibodies were resolved as false-positive by negative Western blot, negative imaging, and PCR identification of Dirofilaria repens.
rationale: A 31-year-old male presented with migratory cellulitis-like plaques and a subcutaneous nodule. Initial screening showed cross-reactive positive IgG ELISA and IHA for E. granulosus, but the western blot confirmation test was negative, and comprehensive sonography and CT scans revealed no hydatid cysts. Histopathological examination of the excised nodule and 12S rRNA PCR sequencing definitively confirmed Dirofilaria repens, ruling out echinococcosis.

step4_condition_matched: Echinococcosis of central nervous system (ruled out)

evidence_items.source_quote: Other infectious workups included blood cultures and fungal (histoplasmosis and cryptococcus), parasitic (toxoplasmosis and echinococcosis), bacterial (syphilis and tuberculosis), and viral (human immunodeficiency virus, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C) studies, which were all negative.

step10_contradiction_notes: Infectious differential diagnosis including echinococcosis was negative and ruled out in favor of neuro-Behçet's syndrome.
rationale: A 20-year-old male presented with headache, visual defects, hemiparesis, and thalamic/brainstem mass lesions. Extensive infectious diagnostic evaluation including parasitic serology for echinococcosis was completely negative. Brain biopsy and clinical criteria established a diagnosis of neuro-Behçet's syndrome, definitively ruling out echinococcosis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Microscopic section showed a cyst wall that was composed of hyalinized fibrous tissue without epithelial lining.
evidence_items.result: NEGATIVE FOR ECHINOCOCCOSIS (hyalinized fibrous tissue without epithelial lining, consistent with splenic pseudocyst)

evidence_items.source_quote: The features confirmed a SP.
A list of differentials was considered that included a splenic hydatid cyst, pancreatic tail pseudocyst, and a mesenteric cyst.

rationale: A 47-year-old woman presented with an expanding splenic cyst initially suspected on ultrasound to likely represent hydatidosis, and managed preoperatively in the differential diagnosis. Splenectomy was performed, and microscopic examination of the cyst wall demonstrated hyalinized fibrous tissue without epithelial lining and absence of cellular atypia or parasitic elements, definitively confirming a non-parasitic splenic pseudocyst (SP) and ruling out hydatid disease. Target condition ruled out; assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The diagnosis of askin's tumor was established histological (Figure 2) on the presence of small cells with scant cytoplasm and focal necrosis, the cells were round and had scant cytoplasm with inconspicuous nucleoli.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathologic and immunohistochemical examination of lung mass
evidence_items.result: CONFIRMED ASKIN TUMOR (positive for NSE and CD99; negative for hydatid cyst)

evidence_items.source_quote: the first diagnosis suspected, within his past history and endemic aspect of hydatid disease in our region was a hydatid cyst of the lung.

rationale: An 11-year-old boy presented with right chest pain and an upper lobe opacity initially suspected to represent a pulmonary hydatid cyst given regional endemicity and past history of hepatic hydatid surgery. Following surgical resection, histopathology and immunohistochemistry (positive for NSE and CD99) definitively established Askin's tumor, ruling out active pulmonary echinococcosis. Target condition ruled out; assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hydatid disease serology was performed to exclude parasitic splenic cyst (PSC) which came out to be negative.

Histopathological assessment of the removed part of the spleen with the cyst revealed primary non-parasitic splenic mesothelial in origin (arrows in Figure 4(A)), there was no squamous metaplasia, there was no evidence of clear septation or trabeculations (Figure 4(A)).
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathologic assessment of resected splenic cyst

rationale: A 13-year-old girl presented with a huge splenic mass. Serologic testing for hydatid disease was explicitly performed to evaluate for parasitic splenic cyst and was negative (E0 contradicted). Subsequent surgical resection and histopathologic assessment with immunohistochemistry confirmed a primary non-parasitic mesothelial splenic cyst. Target condition ruled out; assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A blood sample enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for parasite antibody IgG was positive for S. japonicum and negative for fascioliasis, toxocariasis, trichinellosis, cysticercosis, echinococcosis, and sparganosis.
evidence_items.test_name: Serum parasite antibody IgG ELISA panel
evidence_items.result: NEGATIVE FOR ECHINOCOCCOSIS (positive for S. japonicum)

rationale: A 25-year-old male presented with intermittent headaches and limb weakness due to a brainstem mass. Diagnostic serological evaluation for parasitic etiologies explicitly demonstrated that enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) IgG was negative for echinococcosis (E0 contradicted) and positive for Schistosoma japonicum, which was subsequently confirmed by mucosal biopsy. Target condition ruled out; assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The schistosoma japonicum IgG antibody, echinococcus granulosus antibody, liver fluke antibody test, plasmodium antigen test, and blood smear test were all negative.

rationale: A 47-year-old male presented with recurrent fever, diarrhea, and hepatosplenomegaly. As part of an extensive workup for infectious etiologies, serological testing for Echinococcus granulosus antibody was performed and was explicitly negative (E0 contradicted). Metagenomic next-generation sequencing subsequently identified Leishmania infantum / donovani, confirming kala-azar. Target condition ruled out; assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED. VPD not satisfied -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cystic echinococcosis was excluded serologically.
The patient underwent repeat surgery on the fourth day after the original surgery, and a large choledochal cyst, Todani type 1A, with a diameter of 8-10 cm was found (Fig. 2).

rationale: A 19-year-old female presented with recurrent upper abdominal pain and a large cystic liver lesion. Cystic echinococcosis was investigated in the differential diagnosis and excluded serologically. Repeat surgery definitively diagnosed a Todani type 1A choledochal cyst. The target disease was ruled out (assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS, evidence strength E0_CONTRADICTED) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The schistosoma japonicum IgG antibody, echinococcus granulosus antibody, liver fluke antibody test, plasmodium antigen test, and blood smear test were all negative.

rationale: A 47-year-old male presented with prolonged fever and diarrhea. During an extensive diagnostic workup for fever of unknown origin and hepatosplenomegaly, testing for Echinococcus granulosus antibodies was negative. Diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) was confirmed by blood mNGS and rK39 antibody test. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the US, Doppler US, and pre- and postcontrast abdominal CT findings, a retroperitoneal type CE5 hydatid cyst was diagnosed preoperatively.
Chest CT to look for possible lung metastases was performed after MFH was diagnosed histopathologically.

rationale: A 50-year-old male presented with leg/back pain and a retroperitoneal mass presumed preoperatively to be a type CE5 hydatid cyst. En bloc surgical resection was performed, and histopathological examination proved malignant fibrous histiocytoma (MFH), definitively ruling out hydatid disease. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: It suggested an evaluation of the hydatid cyst. Hence, hydatidAb (IgG) was requested which was negative.
so the pancreatic solid pseudopapillary neoplasm was the most likely diagnosis.

rationale: A 20-year-old female presented with epigastric pain and a cystic epigastric mass. Hydatid cyst was considered in the differential diagnosis and serology (hydatidAb IgG) was explicitly negative. Whipple's procedure was performed, and pathology proved solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pancreas. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 40-year-old male patient was referred to our radiology department for a post-contrast abdominopelvic CT, with the initial impression of a large left upper quadrant localized hydatid cyst (based on a prior abdominal ultrasound).
The CT examination confidently diagnosed a giant pancreatic pseudocyst with trans-spatial extension, concurrent splenic pseudocysts, and perilesional inflammatory changes.

step10_contradiction_notes: Initial ultrasound suspected hydatid cyst, but CT established pancreatic pseudocyst and follow-up imaging showed spontaneous resolution.
rationale: A 40-year-old male with chronic alcohol abuse was referred for CT with an initial ultrasound impression of a large left upper quadrant hydatid cyst. Abdominopelvic CT confidently diagnosed an 18.4 cm giant pancreatic pseudocyst with trans-spatial extension, and conservative management demonstrated spontaneous reduction in cyst size, ruling out hydatid disease. Target disease was evaluated in the differential diagnosis and definitively ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: There was a history of exploratory laparotomy 1 month back for a presumed diagnosis of a hydatid cyst of the liver. A large cystic mass was noted involving the whole left lobe extended into the right lobe. An incisional biopsy was performed, which was reported as poorly differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

step10_contradiction_notes: Presumed hydatid cyst overturned by histopathological biopsy showing undifferentiated malignancy.
rationale: A 20-year-old male presented with a palpable upper abdominal mass. He had undergone an exploratory laparotomy 1 month earlier based on a presumed diagnosis of hepatic hydatid cyst; however, incisional biopsy refuted hydatid disease and demonstrated poorly differentiated carcinoma/sarcoma (ultimately managed with living donor liver transplantation for undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma). Hydatid disease was an initial presumed diagnosis definitively refuted and ruled out by biopsy -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology for entamoeba histolytica and echinococcus granulosus antibodies was negative.
Diagnosis: a ruptured gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess was diagnosed, and a differential diagnosis of perforated viscus was made.

rationale: A 39-year-old male presenting with severe peritonitis and a large hepatic abscess. Serological testing for Echinococcus granulosus antibodies was negative. Exploratory laparotomy confirmed a ruptured gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess. Echinococcosis was evaluated in the differential diagnosis and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic testing with ELISA was done that ruled out hydatid cyst disease.
Based on the symptoms, laboratory investigation, and radiographic findings, the patient was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis complicated by pseudocyst extending into the mediastinum.

rationale: An 18-year-old female presenting with dysphagia, vomiting, and epigastric pain, found to have a cystic mass extending from the pancreas into the posterior mediastinum. Echinococcosis was suspected and evaluated, but ELISA serology was negative. Histopathology and imaging confirmed chronic pancreatitis complicated by a mediastinal pseudocyst -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: tumor markers and echinococcal indirect hemagglutination (IHA) test results were negative.
The lesion was reported histopathologically as BCA displaying high-grade dysplasia.

step10_contradiction_notes: Prior presumptive diagnosis of hydatid cyst from outside CT scan was disproven by negative IHA serology and surgical pathology showing biliary cystadenoma.
rationale: A 37-year-old female with a multiloculated liver cystic lesion previously misdiagnosed and empirically treated as a hydatid cyst. Echinococcal indirect hemagglutination (IHA) test was negative, catheter drainage grew Corynebacterium striatum, and definitive central hepatectomy confirmed biliary cystadenoma (BCA) with high-grade dysplasia on histopathology. Echinococcosis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A provisional diagnosis of a hydatid cyst or a neurogenic tumor was made.
CT-guided trucut biopsy revealed a spindle cell tumor with minimal nuclear atypia, occasional mitotic figure, and necrosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Spindle cell tumor / Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT)

rationale: A 32-year-old female presenting with fever, chest pain, and a large right thoracic paravertebral mass for which a provisional diagnosis of hydatid cyst or neurogenic tumor was considered. Trucut biopsy and complete thoracotomy excision with immunohistochemistry confirmed inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) with strong ALK-1 positivity, ruling out echinococcosis -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Third patient described in report (7-year-old male with persistent pneumonia evaluated for hydatid cyst)

evidence_items.source_quote: His Serum IgG for hydatid cyst was sent which was negative.
Differential diagnoses considered were infected hydatid cyst right lung or congenital cystic pulmonary adenomatoid malformation (CPAM).

rationale: A multi-case report describing three pediatric pulmonary cases. Patient 3, a 7-year-old male with persistent pneumonia and a large cystic lung lesion, was evaluated for an infected hydatid cyst versus CPAM. Serum IgG for hydatid cyst was negative, and right lower lobectomy histopathology definitively confirmed congenital CPAM type 3, ruling out echinococcosis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathological analysis of the excised cyst revealed a biliary epithelial lining with areas of fibrosis and mild chronic inflammation, consistent with a type IV-A choledochal cyst.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of excised bile duct cyst
evidence_items.target_concept: Type IV-A choledochal cyst (non-parasitic biliary epithelium)

evidence_items.source_quote: leading to a preliminary diagnosis of hydatid cyst of the liver with intraductal rupture.

rationale: A 22-year-old female presented with jaundice and abdominal pain. Ultrasound and CT initially led to a preliminary presumptive diagnosis of hepatic hydatid cyst with intraductal rupture. However, subsequent MRCP and intraoperative exploration revealed a type IV-A choledochal cyst, and histopathological analysis confirmed biliary epithelial lining without parasitic elements, definitively excluding hydatid disease. Target disease investigated in differential diagnosis and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatic hydatid disease: Although the patient had no confirmed epidemiological history, the cystic appearance on imaging warranted consideration. However, the solid components and enhancement pattern were not characteristic.

rationale: An 11-year-old boy presented with right upper quadrant pain and a large cystic-solid liver mass diagnosed as undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver (UESL). Hepatic hydatid disease was explicitly considered in the differential diagnosis but ruled out due to non-characteristic solid and enhancement patterns and final histology confirming pediatric hepatic sarcoma. Target disease investigated in differential diagnosis and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: After liver hydatid disease was ruled out by serological examination, and considering that the lesions were too large and prone to rupture, catheter drainage of cyst fluid was performed in both female patients (Figures 1G and 2G).
evidence_items.test_name: Serological testing for liver hydatid disease

evidence_items.source_quote: The histological features and the results of IHC were consistent with a diagnosis of hepatic PEComa.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry of liver mass

rationale: A 64-year-old woman presented with abdominal distension and a 24 cm solid-cystic hepatic mass. Hydatid disease was explicitly evaluated in the differential diagnosis and ruled out by negative serological examination, with subsequent biopsy and immunohistochemistry confirming hepatic PEComa. Target disease investigated in differential diagnosis and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: raising the possibility of a hydatid cyst among the differential diagnoses (Figure 1).
Additionally, serology for hydatid cyst and blood and urine cultures were negative.
Immunohistochemical analysis showed positivity for WT1 and D2-40, supporting the diagnosis of a PIC (Figure 4).
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological and IHC analysis of excised mass

rationale: A 19-year-old male presented with right lower quadrant pain and an 80x50 mm retroperitoneal cystic lesion. CT initially raised the possibility of a hydatid cyst in the differential diagnosis. However, serology for hydatid cyst was negative, and subsequent surgical resection and immunohistochemistry confirmed a peritoneal inclusion cyst (PIC) positive for WT1 and D2-40. Target disease investigated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.
